title: How bands learned tunes and brass band tunes turned to jazz
summary: Interviewer asks about learning new tunes and when brass band pieces such as Didn't He Ramble were jazzed.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: How much time did it usually take for the musicians to learn those tunes? If you had a new tune to put in, did they have to rehearse it very much? That depends. Uh-huh. I mean the blues were fast, all blues tunes were fast. But some of the more complicated things, you know, there were a lot of tunes that, uh, that were played in jazz later, but originally were played, uh, by, by, uh, regular bands, you know, brass bands. Yeah. Uh, which weren't jazz yet, you know? Uh, can you remember when any of those things started to be played by, uh, by, by jazz type bands, the ragtime bands? Well, wait, I got one.
The Butcher? The Butcher cut it down? Didn't he ramble? Didn't he ramble? Uh-huh. That's one of them. Didn't he ramble? Do you remember Muscat ramble? Oh, what's kept-
I mean, before, before the, did the bands always play Muscat ramble?
But I mean, do you remember, uh, when they played them a different way? Jazz band. Always jazz them. Jazz them. Yeah. He made them them. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
